challenge.method: Compare the method-set rule with the adjacent promotion exception and the implicit address-taking rule in Calls at 4262–4266.
challenge.results: An addressable value of T can use the call shorthand for a method of *T while the declared method still belongs to the pointer method set. Promotion from embedded fields could add methods but is excluded here.

limitations: The conclusion covers declared methods and the specified receiver base. Promotion and implicit address-taking have separate rules.
